entities.summary: Salomon, King of Brittany was a count of Rennes and Nantes from 852 and duke of Brittany from 857 until his assassination in 874. In 867, he was granted the counties of Avranches and Coutances, and he used the title king of Brittany intermittently after 868. He was a key figure in the medieval Brittany, playing a crucial role in the region's politics and economy. Salomon's reign was marked by power struggles with neighboring rulers and his efforts to consolidate Brittany's power. His legacy continued through his son, Alan III, who succeeded him as duke of Brittany. The county of Rennes and Nantes remained under Salomon's family rule until the 12th century. The Duchy of Brittany's strategic location in northwest France made it a prized possession for various European powers, including the English and French monarchies. Salomon's diplomatic relations with these powers often involved marriages between his family members and other royal families, securing alliances and trade agreements for Brittany. The King's efforts to establish a strong Brettonic identity were also reflected in his patronage of the monastic order of Saint-Benoît-du-Mont, which played a significant role in the preservation of Brittany's unique cultural heritage. The legacy of Salomon, King of Brittany, can be seen in the continued celebration of the region's patron saint, Saint Yves, who was revered for his missionary work and his role as a symbol of Brittany's cultural identity.
